title: Dave Tough, Hemingway and young musicians who drank
summary: Tough went to Oak Park High, introduced Freeman to Hemingway, and like Wettling and Condon began drinking young; Benny Goodman turned pro at twelve.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Let me ask you, Bud, what school was Dave going to?
Dave Tough was going to Oak Park High School. The same school Hemingway went to, of course, many years before us.
And, incidentally, Dave Tough was one of the first people I ever heard speak about Hemingway. He idolized Hemingway and I remember that six months after
Dave Tough told me about Hemingway, The Sun Also Rises, H. L. Mencken in the American Mercury came up and discovered Hemingway.
Yes. Dave, you know, had this extraordinary literary mind and as you know, Helen, would have become a fine writer if he had lived.
But he had the problem of drinking, I think he sort of just burned himself out.
Did Dave, that problem that Dave had when did that develop? How old was he when that developed?

Well, Dave Tough started to drink, I think, as did many musicians, at the age of 14. George Wettling the same. I say many, that isn't true, but I think there again, as I recall, there were about six different musicians I knew who started to drink at that early age and I think that they just burned themselves out. They could -- maybe a good -- Well, Condon, Eddie Condon certainly started to drink that early because he was a professional player at the age of 14.
There was an extraordinary thing about Benny Goodman that he never got into that. Benny Goodman started to play professionally at the age of 12. He was just an
I knew Benny then, you see, all those years ago.
